title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist (v1 title: Towards an AI co-scientist)
key_finding: Google's Gemini-based multi-agent system generates, critiques and refines hypotheses through a tournament-style evolution; automated evaluations show hypothesis quality keeps improving with more test-time compute, and drug-repurposing candidates for acute myeloid leukemia were validated in vitro.
wow_factor: A team of AI agents that debate each other's ideas produced hypotheses that survived real wet-lab tests.

title: A multi-agent system for automating scientific discovery
key_finding: Robin combines literature-search and data-analysis agents to run the hypothesis–experiment–analysis loop; it proposed and validated ripasudil, a clinically used ROCK inhibitor never previously proposed for dry age-related macular degeneration, and then designed and analysed a follow-up RNA-seq experiment.
wow_factor: An AI system went from literature to a validated drug-repurposing candidate, then designed its own follow-up experiment.

title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
key_finding: The AI Scientist generates ideas, writes code, runs experiments, writes the manuscript and reviews it; one fully AI-generated manuscript passed first-round peer review at a top-tier ML-conference workshop with a 70% acceptance rate.
wow_factor: A machine-written paper passed human peer review, and the system's design is now itself a peer-reviewed Nature paper.
suggested_slide: The AI Scientist: from idea to paper

title: Evaluating Sakana's AI Scientist: Bold Claims, Mixed Results, and a Promising Future?
topic: Risks: reliability of autonomous research agents
key_finding: An independent evaluation found that 42% of the AI Scientist's experiments failed because of coding errors, novelty checks misclassified established ideas as new, and manuscripts had a median of five citations (only 5 of 34 from 2020 or later).
wow_factor: Students can see how independent testing pushes back on bold claims about AI scientists.

title: Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery
key_finding: Kosmos runs for up to 12 hours over 200 agent rollouts, executing on average 42,000 lines of code and reading 1,500 papers per run; independent scientists judged 79.4% of report statements accurate, and collaborators said one 20-cycle run matched about 6 months of their own research.
wow_factor: One overnight run did roughly six months of a researcher's analysis, and every claim is linked to code or a paper.

title: Biomni: A General-Purpose Biomedical AI Agent
key_finding: Biomni builds its action space by mining tools, databases and protocols from tens of thousands of publications across 25 biomedical domains, then combines LLM reasoning, retrieval-augmented planning and code execution; it generalises to tasks such as causal gene prioritisation, microbiome analysis and molecular cloning without task-specific prompt tuning.
wow_factor: An agent that learned its own toolkit by reading the literature points toward a 'Biomni for crops'.

title: CRISPR-GPT for agentic automation of gene-editing experiments
key_finding: The CRISPR-GPT agent helps choose CRISPR systems, design guide RNAs, plan delivery, draft protocols and analyse data; it was used to knock out four genes with Cas12a and to epigenetically activate two genes with dCas9 in human cell lines.
wow_factor: Plant gene-editing design (guides, delivery, assays) could be assisted by the same kind of agent.

title: Autonomous chemical research with large language models
key_finding: Coscientist, driven by GPT-4 and given tools for web and documentation search, code execution and lab automation, designed, planned and ran experiments across six tasks, including successful optimisation of palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reactions.
wow_factor: The first LLM to operate real lab hardware on its own, the starting point for self-driving labs.
suggested_slide: Self-driving labs: when LLMs touch robots

title: An AI Agent for Fully Automated Multi-Omic Analyses
key_finding: AutoBA is an LLM agent that plans and executes end-to-end multi-omic analyses from minimal input; it supports online or local LLM backends for data privacy and uses automated code repair to make runs more stable.
wow_factor: This is a direct ancestor of what students already do with Claude Code: describe the analysis and let the agent write, run and fix the code.

title: Early science acceleration experiments with GPT-5
key_finding: Case studies across mathematics, physics, astronomy, computer science, biology and materials science record where GPT-5 contributed concrete research steps and where it fell short; the collection includes four new mathematical results that the human authors checked.
wow_factor: Frontier-lab models are now documented as contributing to research, with both their successes and their failures reported openly.

title: AlphaEarth Foundations: An embedding field model for accurate and efficient global mapping from sparse label data
key_finding: AlphaEarth Foundations assimilates multi-source Earth-observation data into a general embedding field; its embeddings were the only ones to consistently outperform the other featurisation approaches tested across mapping evaluations without retraining, and annual global layers for 2017–2024 have been released.
wow_factor: A 'virtual satellite' for every field on Earth could become a free environmental covariate for multi-environment trials (G×E).
verified_via: arXiv API record (posted 2025-07-29); public launch reported 2025-07-30/31

title: Large language models in plant biology
key_finding: The review describes how LLM architectures extend beyond human language to DNA, protein and gene-expression sequences, and notes that the plant community had not yet widely adopted these models.
wow_factor: In 2024 the field was described as largely untouched by LLMs, which leaves open ground for this generation of students.

title: From text to traits: exploring the role of large language models in plant breeding
key_finding: The review argues that LLMs could help identify genetic interactions, improve trait prediction and integrate multi-omic, phenotypic and environmental data, and states that their adoption in plant breeding was still largely unexplored.
wow_factor: A breeding-specific roadmap that lists open problems a student thesis could take on.

title: PLLaMa: An Open-source Large Language Model for Plant Science
key_finding: PLLaMa extends LLaMa-2 with more than 1.5 million plant-science articles and is checked by an international panel that includes plant breeders; model checkpoints and code are open.
wow_factor: An open plant-science LLM trained on 1.5 million papers that anyone can download and fine-tune.

title: PlantGPT: An Arabidopsis-Based Intelligent Agent that Answers Questions about Plant Functional Genomics
key_finding: PlantGPT combines retrieval over more than 60,000 plant-research abstracts with Llama3-8B fine-tuned on 13,993 Arabidopsis phenotypes and 23,323 gene functions, and outperforms general LLMs on specialised gene–phenotype questions.
wow_factor: A small 8-billion-parameter model beats general chatbots on plant gene questions, so domain grounding matters more than model size here.

title: PlantScience.ai: An LLM-powered virtual scientist for plant science
key_finding: PlantScience.ai builds a scientific knowledge graph automatically from the plant literature, updates it continuously and grounds each answer in cited primary sources, which targets the terminology errors and missing source traceability of general LLMs.
wow_factor: A citation-aware 'virtual plant scientist' that keeps reading new papers so researchers do not have to read all of them.

title: SeedBench: A Multi-task Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Seed Science
key_finding: SeedBench, built with domain experts to simulate steps of modern seed breeding, was used to evaluate 26 proprietary, open-source and domain-fine-tuned LLMs and found substantial gaps between LLM capability and real seed-science problems.
wow_factor: The first benchmark built around breeding tasks shows that current LLMs are still far from expert breeders.

title: Knowledge-guided Bayesian optimization using pre-trained LLMs speeds up the identification of superior genotypes from germplasm collection
key_finding: In a rice germplasm panel, zero-shot LLM warm-starting from passport data (name, origin, subpopulation) reduced the number of genotypes evaluated before finding the best one for seed number per panicle, with small gains for protein content; Gaussian-process Bayesian optimisation remained strongest when genomic data were available.
wow_factor: An LLM's prior knowledge of cultivar names and origins helps choose which genebank accessions to grow first.
suggested_slide: LLMs choose what to plant next

title: A foundational large language model for edible plant genomes
key_finding: AgroNT, trained on genomes of 48 plant species, reached state-of-the-art predictions of regulatory annotations, promoter/terminator strength and tissue-specific expression, and scored over 10 million in silico cassava mutations; the authors also released the Plants Genomic Benchmark.
wow_factor: The same transformer idea behind chatbots reads crop DNA and scores 10 million mutations before any field trial.
suggested_slide: Language models that read crop DNA

title: Breaking the field phenotyping bottleneck in maize with autonomous robots
key_finding: TerraSentia autonomous ground robots collected in-canopy data from nearly 200,000 experimental units at 142 research fields in the USA and Canada over five years, and delivered validated plant height, ear height, stem diameter and leaf area index at a scale sufficient to dissect genotype × nitrogen interactions.
wow_factor: Robots that phenotype under the canopy at continental scale are the physical layer needed for closed-loop AI breeding.

title: Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT
key_finding: Across 636 citations in 84 ChatGPT-written literature reviews, 55% of GPT-3.5 citations and 18% of GPT-4 citations were fabricated, and 43% and 24% of the real citations, respectively, contained substantive errors.
wow_factor: The error rate dropped sharply between model generations but did not reach zero, which is why every reference in this course is checked against its DOI.

title: Toward autonomous science with agentic artificial intelligence
key_finding: The perspective traces the path from prediction tools (e.g., AlphaFold) to agentic systems (Co-Scientist, Robin, Biomni) and agentic workbenches, and argues that their potential cannot be separated from hallucination, bias, irreproducibility and dual-use risks.
wow_factor: Cell frames agentic AI as a new phase of science and asks for responsible human–AI collaboration.
suggested_slide: Promise and peril of agentic science

title: Bayer pilots unique generative AI tool for agriculture
key_finding: On 14 March 2024 Bayer announced the pilot of an expert GenAI system trained on years of internal data and insights from thousands of trials in its testing network, intended to support agronomists and farmers.
wow_factor: A major seed company turned decades of trial data into an assistant that answers questions in plain language.

title: Bayer's E.L.Y. Wins 'AI-based AgTech Solution of the Year' in 2025 AgTech Breakthrough Awards Program
key_finding: According to Bayer's internal benchmarks, E.L.Y. improves response times to customer questions by 60%, and employees report saving up to four hours per week; the system uses a frontier LLM with retrieval-augmented generation over agronomic data, field-trial results and label guidance.
wow_factor: A domain GenAI system already reports measurable productivity gains for agronomists in the field.
verified_via: press release URL (dated 2025-08-21); metrics are company-reported, not peer-reviewed

title: Anthropic launches Claude Life Sciences to give researchers an AI efficiency boost
key_finding: On 20 October 2025 Anthropic launched Claude for Life Sciences, its first formal entry into the sector, with connectors to scientific tools including Benchling, PubMed and 10x Genomics, aimed at work from literature review and hypothesis generation to data analysis and regulatory drafting.
wow_factor: The coding agent students already use is being connected to lab notebooks, literature databases and single-cell platforms.
